industries: Payments processing, aviation, corporate headquarters and logistics give Atlanta a broad, credential-conscious project market.
intro:
Atlanta quietly runs much of America's commerce: the payment processors of Transaction Alley handle most US card volume, Delta operates the world's busiest airport, and headquarters from Coca-Cola to Home Depot manage global programmes from the metro. Fintech growth has made Scrum credentials valuable; the corporate and logistics base keeps PMP in steady demand, and Georgia's film and healthcare booms add more. We run live online cohorts throughout the year on Atlanta-friendly hours — weekend Saturday–Sunday batches and midweek Wednesday–Thursday batches both — meaning learners in Atlanta attend at ordinary local times, never overnight; the table below shows each upcoming date converted for Atlanta. Either way: live weekend training, exam application support, full-length mock exams, and trainer access until you pass.

Atlanta moves things — freight, payments, passengers, packets — and every one of those flows runs on projects: logistics giants, fintech processors handling most of US card volume, and the corporate headquarters clustered from Midtown to the Perimeter. Program governance is standard across all of them, and certified candidates clear Atlanta's high-volume screening funnels faster. Training is live online across two consecutive days shown in Atlanta local time on this page — no connector traffic to a venue. Georgia compensation for certified project roles is strong against cost of living; the sourced Atlanta entries below carry names and dates. The employer list reflects the logistics-fintech-corporate spread, and processors scaling delivery organizations can certify cohorts privately.
